content: zeroize crate is WASM-compatible (portable pure-Rust volatile-write implementation, not compiler-optimized away) but has known pitfalls unrelated to WASM specifically: Rust move semantics can leave copies of secret data on the stack before the Drop/zeroize runs; Vec/String/CString zeroize only clears current backing-buffer capacity, so any prior reallocation (growth) can leave stale copies of secret bytes in memory that were never zeroized - must pre-allocate exact capacity and avoid growth. wasm-bindgen adds an extra layer: JS-owned vs Rust-owned buffer copies across the JS/WASM boundary are common and not zeroized automatically.
